issue_context.title: New logger API
issue_context.body:
As a breaking change, we can simplify the input by splitting the `logger` option into multiple and dedicated properties:
 
---

After writing my [comments around a simplification suggestion](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4520#discussion_r1084094683) around the `validateLogger` function I have determined that we need to re-think how we deal with this issue.

It was a mistake (that I am responsible for) to accept either an object of options or an instance for the `logger` property. It's a simpler UX, but basically impossible to handle in a concise and maintainable way with the new throwing requirement. I think it is a good idea to introduce the throwing requirement. But I think it means we need to:

1. Deprecate support for `{ logger: <logger_instance> }`.
2. Introduce `{ loggerInstance: <logger_instance> }`.
3. If `loggerInstance` is provided, it takes precedence over `{ logger: <options> }`.

The other avenue is to deprecate `{ logger: <options> }`, but I am quite certain that more people pass in options than they do logger instances. We'd break many more people with this avenue.

_Originally posted by @jsumners in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4520#pullrequestreview-1265646050_
comments: Is this issue still open ? I want to work on this.

>3. If loggerInstance is provided, it takes precedence over `{ logger: <options> }`.

Shouldn't it be an error to provide both? When would you want to pass `logger` if you also pass your own instance?

> Shouldn't it be an error to provide both?

It could be handled as an error, yes.

> When would you want to pass `logger` if you also pass your own instance?

You wouldn't. That's the purpose of the requirement: when the developer passes their own logger instance, but for some reason _also_ passes a set of logger options, then ignore the logger options and only use the passed in instance.
Right, which is why I think it should be an error (or at least a warning, but since this'll go into a major anyways, just erroring seems better) and not silently ignored. 👍
I prefer things to "just work" according to the most likely intention. But if everyone else wants it to error so that folks have to handle errors when starting a server, that's fine by me.

If the function signature gets overloaded so that TypeScript yells at you if you try to specify both, then that would make a runtime error less useful, as it could be caught in the type check stage.

And its pretty obvious that `loggerInstance` should take precedence, so I don't think there's really a need to throw an error (generally I do prefer to throw errors as early as possible otherwise, so generally I would agree with @SimenB here, but I think I'm actually leaning towards @jsumners on this specific one)

>And its pretty obvious that loggerInstance should take precedence, so I don't think there's really a need to throw an error (generally I do prefer to throw errors as early as possible otherwise, so generally I would agree with @SimenB here, but I think I'm actually leaning towards @jsumners on this specific one)

If that's documented, I think is ok to do it, otherwise can lead to ambiguity, especially if not using TS to error this on the type checking.
Can I give this a try?
Was it considered to just add a `loggerInstance` to the logger options input? If its passed, that takes precedent.

No, the loggerInstance is separate from logger. For example, if you pass a logger instance such as pino to loggerInstance and a configuration to logger, the pino instance passed will take precedence.
